newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bunds futures spiral down again as supports fail.
newsitem.headline: Bunds futures spiral down again as supports fail.

text.p: German Bund futures skidded lower in late trade on Thursday as, for the second session in a row, a wave of selling overcame techniacl supports.
Traders said after the DTB June futures took out key long-term trendline support late on Wednesday, the next key aid for this session at 100.81/83 also crumbled.
"Things certainly don't look very good here," said one futures broker based in Frankfurt.
The June contract, which crunched through 101.81 support to hit a low of 100.63 in late business, was trading 42 basis points lower at 100.75 by 1455 GMT.
"The uptrend is broken, and has been confirmed as broken," said broker said.
But analysts said that aside from nervousness about Germany's deficit difficulties, there was no other clear reason for the recent sharp sell-off in Bund futures.
They said the market was now focussing on the 100.30 area -- where a Fibonacci retracement level comes in -- as the next possible support region.
"I would be looking for the contract to bounce there and settle into a 100.30 to 101.00 range," said one trader.
In the cash market 10-year Bunds proved quite resilient.
By 1509 GMT the benchmark was quoted at 100.53 for a bid yield of 5.922 percent, down 19 ticks on the day.
For futures, traders said the key for the next few sessions would be Thursday's closing level.
If the contract ends below 101.00 but above 100.80, the recent slide would at least be slowed, they said. But it would take a close above 101.00 to attract real buying interest into the market.
"People are very nervous," said one trader.
